findings.summary: Malformed npm run commands can bypass package-script validation
evidence: packageScriptName now returns script || undefined for npm run instead of rejecting when no script is named.

preflightRequiredVerificationCommands only calls assertPackageScript when a script name is returned, so a required command such as npm run --silent is accepted and executes npm script-listing behavior rather than the configured verification script.
The removed tests previously covered npm run with no script and asserted rejection; replacement tests do not cover this path.

findings.summary: Investigation label projection no longer recognizes valid non-uppercase verdict formatting
evidence: The previous implementation used a case-insensitive regex allowing whitespace and both decompose/decomposed, then passed the parsed outcome to canonical mapping.
The replacement checks only exact **Verdict**: INVALID; lowercase or whitespace-variant INVALID and every DECOMPOSED verdict fall through to workflow:ready-to-build.
An investigation report with **Verdict**: DECOMPOSED or normal lowercase formatting can therefore project a build-ready label instead of invalid/decomposed, changing workflow routing.

findings.summary: setWorkflowLabel no longer validates issueNumber before interpolating it into the GitHub API path
evidence: The previous positive safe-integer check was removed from setWorkflowLabel.

The changed code directly constructs `${this.#apiRoot}/issues/${issueNumber}` and `${this.#apiRoot}/issues/${issueNumber}/labels`; JavaScript callers or deserialized state can supply non-number values despite the TypeScript annotation, allowing path/query characters or malformed values to reach the transport.
projectEvent and #addMissingLabels retain the same validation/normalization pattern, demonstrating that this method's removed guard is a regression rather than an intentional API contract change.
